meta.description: Batch program that generates periodic credit card account statements from transaction data, producing output in both plain text and HTML formats.
meta.process_description: CBSTM03A reads transaction data from a transaction file and cross-references it with customer and account data to produce formatted account statements. For each credit card account, it collects up to 10 transactions per card (supporting up to 51 cards in a batch run), calculates total expenditure, and formats a complete statement including customer name, address, account ID, current balance, FICO credit score, and an itemised transaction summary. The program produces two output files simultaneously: a fixed-width 80-character plain text statement file and a styled HTML statement file suitable for digital delivery or web rendering. It delegates all physical file I/O operations (open, close, read, write) to the subroutine CBSTM03B, acting as the orchestrating controller for the statement generation process.

files.STMTFILE: Plain text output file containing formatted account statements (80-character fixed width records) for customer mailing or archival
files.HTMLFILE: HTML-formatted output file containing styled account statements suitable for digital/web delivery to customers
files.TRNXFILE: Input transaction file containing credit card transaction records used as the source data for statement generation
files.XREFFILE: Cross-reference file linking card numbers to account numbers, used to associate transactions with the correct account
files.CUSTFILE: Customer master file containing personal details (name, address) used to populate the customer-facing sections of the statement
files.ACCTFILE: Account master file containing account-level financial data including current balance and FICO credit score

business_rules: Each account statement must include customer identification details (name and full address), account ID, current balance, and FICO credit score.
The transaction summary section lists each transaction with its unique transaction ID, transaction details/description, and individual transaction amount in USD.
A total expenditure figure is calculated and printed at the bottom of the transaction summary, representing the sum of all transactions in the statement period.
Statements are generated simultaneously in two formats (plain text and HTML) to support both print/mail and digital delivery channels.
The program supports batch processing of up to 51 credit card accounts per run, with a maximum of 10 transactions stored in memory per card before flushing to the statement output.
All file operations (open, read, write, close) for source data files are delegated to the CBSTM03B subroutine, enforcing a separation between statement formatting logic and file I/O handling.
The program logs the executing JCL job name and step name at startup, providing an audit trail identifying which scheduled batch job produced the statements.
Transaction amounts are displayed with a sign indicator to distinguish credits from debits on the customer statement.
The HTML statement uses the bank identity 'Bank of XYZ' with address '410 Terry Ave N, Seattle WA 99999', indicating a configurable bank branding requirement for digital statements.

variables.name: FD-STMTFILE-REC
variables.description: A single 80-character line of a plain-text account statement destined for the STMTFILE output. Each record written here represents one printed line on the paper/mailed statement sent to the customer.

variables.name: FD-HTMLFILE-REC
variables.description: A single 100-character line of an HTML-formatted account statement destined for the HTMLFILE output. Each record written here represents one line of HTML markup that will be rendered in a browser or email client for digital statement delivery.

variables.name: COMP-VARIABLES
variables.description: Group of binary integer counters used to track transaction processing statistics and pagination/layout control during statement generation.

variables.name: CR-CNT
variables.description: Running count of credit transactions processed during the current batch run. Used to track how many payments or credits appeared on customer statements, supporting reconciliation and audit reporting.

variables.name: TR-CNT
variables.description: Running count of all transactions (both debits and credits) processed during the current batch run. Provides a total transaction volume figure for audit and reconciliation purposes.

variables.name: CR-JMP
variables.description: Jump or offset counter associated with credit transaction positioning, used internally to control the layout or indexing of credit entries when building the statement output.

variables.name: TR-JMP
variables.description: Jump or offset counter associated with total transaction positioning, used internally to control the layout or indexing of transaction entries when building the statement output.

variables.name: COMP3-VARIABLES
variables.description: Group of packed-decimal numeric variables used for high-precision financial calculations during statement generation.

variables.name: WS-TOTAL-AMT
variables.description: Running total of all transaction amounts accumulated for the current account's statement period. This is the figure that becomes the total expenditure printed at the bottom of the transaction summary section of the customer's statement.

variables.name: MISC-VARIABLES
variables.description: Group of miscellaneous working-storage variables used to control transaction file reading and track processing state across the batch statement generation run.

variables.name: WS-FL-DD
variables.description: The JCL DD name of the transaction input file (TRNXFILE). This value is passed to the CBSTM03B subroutine to identify which file to read transaction records from when building customer statements.

variables.name: WS-TRN-AMT
variables.description: Holds the dollar amount of the individual transaction currently being processed. Used as a working field to accumulate into WS-TOTAL-AMT and to format the transaction amount for printing on the statement.

variables.name: WS-SAVE-CARD
variables.description: Stores the card number of the account currently being processed. When the next transaction record carries a different card number, this mismatch signals that processing has moved to a new customer account, triggering statement finalization and output for the previous account.

variables.name: END-OF-FILE
variables.description: A flag that indicates whether all transaction records in the input file have been read. Set to 'Y' when the last transaction has been processed, signaling the program to finalize and output the last account's statement and then terminate the batch run.

variables.name: WS-M03B-AREA
variables.description: Communication area used to pass instructions and data between the main statement generation program (CBSTM03A) and the file I/O subroutine (CBSTM03B). All file operations—opening, reading, writing, and closing the source and output files—are requested by populating this area and calling CBSTM03B.

variables.name: WS-M03B-DD
variables.description: The JCL DD name identifying which file the CBSTM03B subroutine should operate on (e.g., TRNXFILE, XREFFILE, CUSTFILE, ACCTFILE, STMTFILE, HTMLFILE). This tells the subroutine which data source or output destination is involved in the requested operation.

variables.name: WS-M03B-OPER
variables.description: A single-character operation code instructing the CBSTM03B subroutine what file action to perform. Valid values are O (Open), C (Close), R (Read sequentially), K (Read by Key), W (Write), and Z (Rewrite), covering the full lifecycle of file access needed during statement generation.

variables.name: M03B-OPEN
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when WS-M03B-OPER is 'O', meaning the program is requesting CBSTM03B to open a file before reading or writing statement data.

variables.name: M03B-CLOSE
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when WS-M03B-OPER is 'C', meaning the program is requesting CBSTM03B to close a file after all reading or writing for that file is complete.

variables.name: M03B-READ
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when WS-M03B-OPER is 'R', meaning the program is requesting CBSTM03B to read the next sequential record from a file (e.g., reading the next transaction from TRNXFILE).

variables.name: M03B-READ-K
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when WS-M03B-OPER is 'K', meaning the program is requesting CBSTM03B to read a specific record by key (e.g., looking up a customer record by customer ID or an account record by account ID).

variables.name: M03B-WRITE
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when WS-M03B-OPER is 'W', meaning the program is requesting CBSTM03B to write a new statement line record to either the plain-text or HTML output file.

variables.name: M03B-REWRITE
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when WS-M03B-OPER is 'Z', meaning the program is requesting CBSTM03B to update (rewrite) an existing record in a file, used when modifying previously written data.

variables.name: WS-M03B-RC
variables.description: The return code sent back from the CBSTM03B subroutine after each file operation. The main program inspects this value to determine whether the operation succeeded or failed, enabling error handling such as aborting the batch if a critical file cannot be opened or read.

variables.name: WS-M03B-KEY
variables.description: The search key value passed to CBSTM03B when performing a keyed file read (M03B-READ-K). For example, this would hold a customer ID or account ID when looking up a specific customer or account record to populate the statement.

variables.name: WS-M03B-KEY-LN
variables.description: The length of the key value stored in WS-M03B-KEY. This tells CBSTM03B exactly how many characters of the key field are significant when performing a keyed lookup, accommodating keys of varying lengths across different files.

variables.name: WS-M03B-FLDT
variables.description: A 1000-character data buffer used to transfer file record contents between the CBSTM03B subroutine and the main program. When reading, CBSTM03B places the retrieved record here (e.g., a customer record or account record); when writing, the main program places the formatted statement line here for CBSTM03B to write to the output file.

Each sub-field (ST-LINE0 through ST-LINE9) represents a distinct section of the printed statement, from the header banner through customer details, account information, and transaction summary.

variables.name: WS-TRNX-TABLE
variables.description: In-memory batch processing table that holds transaction data for up to 51 credit card accounts simultaneously. As transactions are read from the input file, they are accumulated here before being flushed to the statement output, enabling efficient batch statement generation without repeated file I/O.

variables.name: WS-CARD-TBL
variables.description: One slot in the in-memory table representing a single credit card account being processed in the current batch run. Up to 51 card accounts can be held in memory at once, each with their associated transactions, before statements are generated and written to output files.

variables.name: WS-CARD-NUM
variables.description: The 16-digit credit card number identifying which card account this table slot belongs to. Used to group transactions by card during batch processing so that all charges for a given card are consolidated onto a single statement.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-TBL
variables.description: A sub-table holding up to 10 individual transactions for a single card account in memory. When this limit is reached, the accumulated transactions are flushed to the statement output, enforcing the batch processing limit of 10 transactions per card before writing.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-NUM
variables.description: The unique 16-character transaction identifier for a single transaction stored in the in-memory batch table. This ID is later printed on the customer statement so the cardholder can reference a specific transaction when querying a charge.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-REST
variables.description: The remaining transaction detail fields (type, category, source, description, amount, merchant information, and timestamps) stored as a single block for one transaction in the in-memory batch table. This data is used to populate the transaction description and amount columns on the customer statement.

variables.name: WS-TRN-TBL-CNTR
variables.description: Counter table that tracks how many transactions have been accumulated in memory for each of the 51 possible card accounts currently being processed. Used to determine when a card's transaction buffer is full and statement output must be written.

variables.name: WS-TRN-TBL-CTR
variables.description: A single counter entry corresponding to one card account slot in the batch table, tracking how many transactions have been loaded for that account. When this reaches 10, the program flushes the transactions to the statement output files.

variables.name: WS-TRCT
variables.description: The actual numeric count of transactions currently held in memory for one specific card account. Incremented each time a transaction is added to that account's buffer and reset after the transactions are written to the statement, controlling the batch flush cycle.

variables.name: PSAPTR
variables.description: A system-level pointer to the Prefixed Save Area (PSA) — a z/OS operating system control block. Used internally by the program to navigate the system control block chain in order to retrieve the JCL job name and step name for audit logging of which scheduled batch job produced the statements.

variables.name: BUMP-TIOT
variables.description: A numeric working field used to perform pointer arithmetic when navigating the z/OS Task I/O Table (TIOT) control block chain. Allows the program to locate the correct memory address of the TIOT in order to extract the JCL job and step names for audit trail purposes.

variables.name: TIOT-INDEX
variables.description: A pointer overlay on the BUMP-TIOT field that reinterprets the calculated numeric address as a memory pointer to the Task I/O Table (TIOT). Enables the program to directly access the TIOT control block to read the JCL job name and step name for statement audit logging.

variables.name: ALIGN-PSA
variables.description: A large binary numeric field used to hold and align the absolute memory address of the z/OS Prefixed Save Area (PSA) during the system control block navigation process. Required to correctly locate the PSA so the program can retrieve the JCL job name for audit logging.

variables.name: PSA-BLOCK
variables.description: A mapped representation of the z/OS Prefixed Save Area (PSA) system control block. The program reads this structure to navigate to the Task Control Block (TCB), which ultimately leads to the Task I/O Table containing the JCL job and step names used in the statement audit trail.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Padding representing the first 536 bytes of the PSA control block that are not needed by this program. Skipped over to position correctly at the TCB pointer field within the PSA structure.

variables.name: TCB-POINT
variables.description: A pointer within the PSA block that holds the memory address of the current Task Control Block (TCB). Used to navigate from the PSA to the TCB as part of the chain of system control blocks needed to retrieve the JCL job name for audit logging.

variables.name: TCB-BLOCK
variables.description: A mapped representation of the z/OS Task Control Block (TCB) system structure. The program reads this to locate the Task I/O Table (TIOT) pointer, which contains the JCL job name and step name recorded in the statement audit trail.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Padding representing the first 12 bytes of the TCB control block that are not relevant to this program. Skipped over to position correctly at the TIOT pointer field within the TCB structure.

variables.name: TIOT-POINT
variables.description: A pointer within the TCB block that holds the memory address of the Task I/O Table (TIOT). Used to navigate to the TIOT so the program can read the JCL job name and step name that identify which scheduled batch job produced the credit card statements.

variables.name: TIOT-BLOCK
variables.description: A mapped representation of the z/OS Task I/O Table (TIOT) header, containing the JCL job name and step names of the currently executing batch job. The program reads this at startup to capture the audit trail information identifying which scheduled job produced the credit card statements.

variables.name: TIOTNJOB
variables.description: The 8-character JCL job name of the batch job currently executing the statement generation run. Extracted from the operating system's Task I/O Table and logged at program startup to provide an audit trail identifying which scheduled batch job produced the credit card statements.

variables.name: TIOTJSTP
variables.description: The 8-character JCL job step name of the specific step within the batch job that is executing the statement generation. Extracted from the Task I/O Table and logged at startup alongside the job name to provide a precise audit trail for the statement production run.

variables.name: TIOTPSTP
variables.description: The 8-character JCL procedure step name within the batch job step, extracted from the Task I/O Table. Provides additional granularity in the audit trail when the batch statement job is invoked via a JCL catalogued procedure rather than an inline step.

variables.name: TIOT-ENTRY
variables.description: A mapped representation of a single DD (Data Definition) entry within the Task I/O Table. Used to iterate through the TIOT entries to locate and validate the DD names of the files used in the statement generation run, supporting file allocation verification and audit purposes.

variables.name: TIOT-SEG
variables.description: The main segment of a single TIOT DD entry, containing the length, DD name, and Unit Control Block address for one allocated dataset. Used to identify and validate the file allocations (such as STMTFILE, TRNXFILE, etc.) associated with the batch statement job.

variables.name: TIO-LEN
variables.description: The length byte of a TIOT DD entry, indicating the size of this particular entry in the Task I/O Table. Used when iterating through TIOT entries to correctly advance to the next DD entry during file allocation inspection.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Reserved/unused bytes within the TIOT DD entry structure that are not relevant to the statement generation program. Padding to maintain correct alignment with the operating system control block layout.

variables.name: TIOCDDNM
variables.description: The 8-character DD name from a TIOT entry, identifying a specific file allocation in the JCL for the batch statement job (e.g. STMTFILE, TRNXFILE, ACCTFILE). Used to verify that the required input and output files are correctly allocated before statement processing begins.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Reserved/unused bytes within the TIOT DD entry structure following the DD name. Padding to maintain correct alignment with the operating system control block layout.

variables.name: UCB-ADDR
variables.description: The 3-byte Unit Control Block (UCB) address within a TIOT DD entry, pointing to the physical device or dataset allocated to this DD name. Used to determine whether a DD entry has an actual device allocated (non-null) or is a dummy/unallocated entry.

variables.name: NULL-UCB
variables.description: Condition flag that is true when the UCB address in a TIOT entry is all binary zeros (LOW-VALUES), indicating that this DD entry has no physical device or dataset allocated. Used to skip over unallocated DD entries when scanning the TIOT for valid file allocations.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Padding bytes at the end of the TIOT entry structure, maintaining correct alignment with the operating system's TIOT layout when iterating through DD entries during file allocation inspection.

variables.name: END-OF-TIOT
variables.description: Condition flag that is true when the current TIOT entry is all binary zeros (LOW-VALUES), signalling that there are no more DD entries in the Task I/O Table. Used to terminate the loop that scans TIOT entries for file allocation verification during batch statement job startup.

paragraphs.name: 0000-START
paragraphs.description: This paragraph acts as the central dispatch router for the file I/O subroutine CBSTM03B, directing each incoming file operation request to the correct file-handling routine based on which file and operation type has been requested by the calling program CBSTM03A.

paragraphs.name: 1000-MAINLINE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph is the main orchestration loop of the statement generation process. It drives the end-to-end batch cycle: for each cross-reference entry found, it retrieves the matching customer and account details, builds the statement structure, resets the expenditure total, and collects the associated transactions — then closes all input and output files once every record has been processed.

paragraphs.name: 9999-GOBACK
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal termination point of the statement generation batch program, returning control to the operating system or calling process once all account statements have been produced.

paragraphs.name: 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the next card-to-account cross-reference record from the cross-reference file, enabling the program to link a credit card number to its corresponding customer account. It handles end-of-file and error conditions to ensure safe, controlled processing of all card associations in the batch run.

paragraphs.name: 2000-CUSTFILE-GET
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the full customer personal record from the customer master file using the customer ID linked to the card being processed. It ensures the statement can be populated with the customer's name and address details, and abends the job if the customer record cannot be found.

paragraphs.name: 3000-ACCTFILE-GET
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the full account record from the account master file using the account ID obtained from the card cross-reference lookup. This provides the financial details (current balance, credit limit, FICO score) needed to populate the customer's statement.

paragraphs.name: 4000-TRNXFILE-GET
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves and outputs all transactions for the current credit card account being processed, calculates the total expenditure for the statement period, and writes the transaction summary footer to both the plain text and HTML statement files.

paragraphs.name: 5000-CREATE-STATEMENT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph assembles and writes a complete formatted account statement for a single customer, combining personal identification details, address, account financials, and credit score into both plain text and HTML output files. It acts as the orchestrating step that transforms raw customer and account data into a customer-ready statement document.

paragraphs.name: 5100-WRITE-HTML-HEADER
paragraphs.description: This paragraph constructs and writes the opening HTML header section of a customer credit card statement, establishing the page structure, bank branding, and account identification before the transaction detail body is rendered. It sequentially outputs each pre-defined HTML line — including document metadata, styling, bank identity, and the customer's account number — to the HTML statement output file.

paragraphs.name: 5100-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the enclosing processing routine, providing a clean termination marker that allows the batch statement generation flow to return control to the calling logic after completing its work.

paragraphs.name: 5200-WRITE-HTML-NMADBS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph renders the customer-facing section of the HTML statement, writing the account holder's name, full postal address, account identifier, current balance, and FICO credit score into the HTML output file, surrounded by structured HTML table markup to produce a professionally formatted digital statement.

paragraphs.name: 5200-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as a formal exit point for the enclosing processing routine, providing a clean termination anchor that allows the batch statement generation logic to return control to the calling section in an orderly and structured manner.

paragraphs.name: 6000-WRITE-TRANS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph renders a single transaction line onto both the plain text statement and the HTML statement simultaneously, ensuring each transaction's unique identifier, description, and amount are presented to the customer in both delivery formats.

paragraphs.name: 8100-FILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the entry point for the file-opening phase of the batch statement run, immediately redirecting control to the specific routine responsible for opening the transaction source file first.

paragraphs.name: 8100-TRNXFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph initialises access to the credit card transaction source file and reads the very first transaction record, bootstrapping the statement generation batch run. It validates that the file is accessible and contains data, then anchors the process to the first card account found before handing control back to the main processing loop.

paragraphs.name: 8200-XREFFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the card-to-account cross-reference file, which is essential for linking each credit card transaction to the correct customer account during statement generation. If the file cannot be opened, the batch job is immediately aborted to prevent producing incomplete or incorrect statements.

paragraphs.name: 8300-CUSTFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the customer master file so that personal details (name and address) can be retrieved for inclusion in account statements. If the file cannot be opened, the batch job is immediately aborted to prevent statements being generated without customer data.

paragraphs.name: 8400-ACCTFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the Account Master File so that the statement generation process can retrieve account-level financial data (current balance and FICO credit score) for each customer. If the file cannot be opened successfully, the batch job is immediately aborted to prevent statements being produced with missing or incomplete account information.

paragraphs.name: 8500-READTRNX-READ
paragraphs.description: This paragraph reads and accumulates credit card transactions from the input transaction file into an in-memory batch table, grouping them by card account. It detects when processing moves to a new card account, finalises the transaction count for the previous card, and continues reading until all transactions are exhausted or an error occurs.

paragraphs.name: 8599-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph finalises the recording of the total transaction count for the current card account being processed, then resets the file pointer to the cross-reference file and loops back to the start of the main processing cycle to handle the next card account in the batch.

paragraphs.name: 9100-TRNXFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the transaction input file once all transaction records have been read and processed for statement generation. It ensures the file is properly released and halts the entire batch job if the closure fails, protecting data integrity.

paragraphs.name: 9200-XREFFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph closes the card-to-account cross-reference file once all transaction-to-account lookups have been completed for the batch run. It ensures the cross-reference data source is properly released, and aborts the entire batch job if the file cannot be closed cleanly.

paragraphs.name: 9300-CUSTFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph closes the customer master file after all required customer personal details (names and addresses) have been retrieved for statement generation. It ensures the file is properly released and handles any unexpected closure failures by halting the batch job with an error.

paragraphs.name: 9400-ACCTFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the account master file after all account financial data (balances and FICO scores) has been retrieved for statement generation. It delegates the physical file closure to the I/O subroutine and halts the entire batch job if the file cannot be closed cleanly, protecting data integrity.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles unrecoverable fatal errors by logging a termination notice and forcing an immediate abnormal end (abend) of the batch statement generation job, ensuring the failure is visible to operations teams for investigation.
